finding.summary: The `output` "regression guard for #660" cannot fail on the regression it claims to guard
finding.evidence: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:157-164 comments itself as "Regression guard for #660" and asserts `output({a:1},'json')` prints the body. But the actual regression this PR fixes lives at the ~30 call sites that used to pass `opts.quiet` (e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:83, cells.ts:26). After the signature change, `output` unconditionally prints regardless of quiet, so the assertion holds trivially and would ALSO have held on the old code (which was called with quiet=false in this test's shape). If someone reintroduced suppression at a call site (`if (!opts.quiet) output(...)`) or re-added a defaulted `quiet` param, this test still passes. Nothing in packages/cli/test parses `--quiet` through a command action and asserts the body is still written to stdout — namespaces.test.ts:11 shows the createProgram()-based harness exists to do exactly that but only inspects option metadata. The comment's fallback claim ("a caller that tries to pass one fails to compile") is a type-level assertion never exercised by any test (no expectTypeError / ts-expect-error case).

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that nothing in packages/cli/test parses --quiet through a command action and asserts the body still reaches stdout. That exact test exists in the cited file: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:180-279 is a describe block ('--quiet does not suppress the body or the error envelope') that builds a real commander program via createProgram() + registerDocsCommand + registerSheetsCommand (lines 232-237) and runs parseAsync with the --quiet flag (lines 239-241). Only global fetch is stubbed (222-230); commander option parsing, the command actions, and the formatter are real. It asserts: `docs list --quiet` prints the body once with exit code 0 (243-251); `sheets cells get ... --quiet` prints the body (253-260); `docs list --quiet --format csv` prints CSV (262-266); and an HTTP 500 under --quiet prints the error envelope on stderr with exitCode 1 (268-278). Reintroducing `if (!opts.quiet) output(...)` at packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:83 would fail the `toHaveBeenCalledOnce` assertion at output.test.ts:246, so the guard is not vacuous. The finding's quoted evidence also does not match the file: lines 157-165 are the plain 'prints the body' unit test, and the 'Regression guard for #660' comment is at 173-179, where it explicitly says direct output() assertions cannot catch the regression and the guard must drive a real command.

finding.summary: Deleted quiet test for `outputError` replaced by an unrelated case; the new "errors print even under quiet" contract is untested
finding.evidence: The diff removes `it('honors quiet by exiting 1 without emitting stderr')` and substitutes `it('stringifies non-Error throwables')` (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:137-141), which exercises the pre-existing `String(error)` branch, not the changed behavior. The new documented contract in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:44-51 — that the error envelope survives `--quiet` — has no test at any level: every remaining outputError test calls it directly with no quiet notion, and no command-level test runs a failing command with `--quiet` to assert stderr is non-empty and exitCode is 1. Net effect: a behavior change (quiet no longer silences errors) shipped with strictly less coverage of quiet than before.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the "errors print even under --quiet" contract has no test at any level, and specifically that "no command-level test runs a failing command with --quiet to assert stderr is non-empty and exitCode is 1". That test exists in the very file cited: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:268-278, inside the describe block '--quiet does not suppress the body or the error envelope' (line 180), which is explicitly documented as the regression guard for this contract (comment at lines 173-179). The test stubs fetch with a 500 (lines 222-230), drives a real commander program via createProgram() + registerDocsCommand (lines 232-241) with the '--quiet' flag, then asserts stdout was NOT written, stderr was called once, the parsed envelope equals {code:'ERROR', message:'HTTP 500'}, and process.exitCode === 1. This is not over-mocked: only global fetch is stubbed; the real failure path runs through docs.ts:117-121 (`throw new Error('HTTP 500')` -> `outputError(e)`) into formatter.ts:52-58. '--quiet' is a genuinely registered global option (root.ts:55, typed at root.ts:19), so the flag is really parsed rather than silently dropped, and the assertion at line 272 would fail if quiet-suppression were reintroduced at the call site. Sibling tests at lines 243-266 cover the `output` half of the same contract under --quiet. The reviewer's observation is accurate only for the describe('outputError') block at lines 95-146; it misses the command-level block further down the same file.
